simple.meaning: אַלְגּוּמִּים (ʼalgûwmmîym) is a Hebrew object word meaning “sticks of algum wood.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.

definitions.full: H418. algummim אֲלְגּוּמִים noun [masculine] plural a tree (foreign & obscure) always with עֲצֵי , perhaps sandal-wood: — 2Chr 2:7 וְא בְּרוֺשִׁים אֲרָזִים ׳עֲצֵי (from Lebanon); אַ ׳עֲצֵי 9:10 (|| יְקָרָה אֶבֶן ; both from Ophir); compare 9:11 , see following

occurrences.englishText: “Now therefore send me a man skillful to work in gold, in silver, in bronze, in iron, and in purple, crimson, and blue, and who knows how to engrave engravings, to be with the skillful men who are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.

The servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum trees‡ possibly Indian sandalwood, which has nice grain and a pleasant scent and is good for woodworking and precious stones.

The king used algum tree wood to make terraces for Yahweh’s house and for the king’s house, and harps and stringed instruments for the singers. There were none like these seen before in the land of Judah.
